inventory: Write a reusable C++ replenishment-alert CLI. A TSV file contains SKU and on-hand integer quantity per observation, in order, without a header. Each SKU begins armed. Emit the SKU in an alert list on its first observation at or below 2, then suppress repeats until that SKU reaches at least 5. Report only entries into low stock. Write the alerts as a JSON array of SKU strings in observation order. Arguments: input TSV, destination JSON. Reject missing input.
sensors: Write a reusable C++ tool for greenhouse operators. Read a TSV log with no header: sensor ID and temperature in whole degrees per observation. Each sensor starts normal. On reaching 30 or higher, append a warning for that sensor exactly once. Re-arm it only when it cools to 25 or below. Write a JSON array of one-based input row numbers at which warnings started, in order. Arguments: input TSV, destination JSON. Reject missing input.
finance: Write a reusable C++ payment reconciliation CLI. Read a TSV with no header containing ledger side (book or bank), reference, and signed amount in integer cents. Match equal reference and amount across opposite sides one-to-one, consuming the earliest unmatched opposite row first. Return the one-based row numbers still unmatched, in original order, as a JSON array. Arguments: source TSV, destination JSON. Reject missing input.
build: Write a reusable C++ parallel-build planner. The input is one JSON object mapping each target name to an array of prerequisite target names. Write a JSON array of build waves: every target ready at the beginning of a wave goes into it, sorted alphabetically; their dependents can start only in a later wave. Repeated prerequisites count once. A cycle or an undeclared prerequisite is an error: exit nonzero and leave the fresh output absent. Arguments: input JSON, destination JSON. Reject missing input.
gzip: Build a reusable C++ command-line utility that takes a gzip archive and a destination file and writes the original bytes. Concatenated gzip members must all be decoded in order. Reject missing input and a broken checksum with a nonzero exit. Arguments: archive, destination.
queue: Write a reusable C++17 header-only library for a waiting list. Deliver waitlist.hpp defining class Waitlist with public bool join(const std::string&), bool cancel(const std::string&) and std::optional<std::string> take(). Join appends a name unless it is already waiting. Cancel removes a waiting name. Both return whether the list changed. Take removes and returns the oldest waiting name, or an empty optional. A cancelled or served name can rejoin at the back. I will include the header in another program; no CLI or file inputs are needed.
